scenes.title: One list, then every finite list

beats.say: Watch three colored tiles — one, two, three — flip through a tail-recursive list reversal by moving each head into an accumulator. Testing checks that one list reverses to three, two, one. Lean 4 lets us prove the algorithm matches the specification for every finite list.

Try induction directly with an empty accumulator and the proof gets stuck: after moving one element, the recursive call carries a non-empty accumulator that the hypothesis cannot match. Generalize the theorem to hold for any starting accumulator, and the inductive regrouping snaps together cleanly for both base and step cases.

Why can you trust a Lean proof — even one written by an AI? Because tactics and search only build a formal proof term. Before Lean accepts the theorem, its tiny trusted kernel checks every single type rule from first principles. One small kernel. Infinite certainty.
